Definition: from a prolonged form of φύρω (to mix a liquid with a solid; perhaps akin to G5453 through the idea of swelling in bulk), mean to knead; a mass of dough:--lump.
BiblicalUsage: Phyrama is a lump of dough, the whole mass from one handful of meal. Paul says a little leaven leavens the whole lump in 1 Corinthians 5:6, and calls believers a new lump in 1 Corinthians 5:7. In Romans 11:16 the lump is holy if the firstfruit is holy, and in Romans 9:21 the potter makes from the same lump one vessel to honour and another to dishonour.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the lump teaches me that small things spread — leaven through dough, holiness through a people, and the potter's right over the clay. My position is that God claims the whole lump, not just the first pinch.
